name: Drought
value: Sudan harvest hit; no famine declared
summary: El Niño drought cuts Sudan's harvest, raising famine risk; no new famine declared or exporter harvest failure
state: An IPC alert in mid-October warned that El Niño-driven drought on top of conflict raises famine risk in parts of Darfur and Kordofan, with near record-poor harvests expected nationwide (IRC, 13 Oct). Sudan's July–September rains were the lowest in more than three decades, and some Gedaref and North Kordofan farmers expected a quarter of normal yields (Reuters via TimesLIVE, 23 Oct). Severe drought in a major crop region keeps this at Watch; searches on 13 Nov found no new drought-driven famine declaration or major exporter harvest failure.
for_you: Farming households and displaced people in Darfur and Kordofan are most exposed, as poor harvests push up local food prices. Drought in exporting regions tends to show up in global grain prices months later.
rubric_hit: Watch: severe drought in a major crop region (Sudan's rain-fed belt); no drought-driven famine declaration or major exporter harvest failure

sources.title: International Rescue Committee — War and El Niño-driven drought deplete food stocks, pushing Sudan further towards famine
TimesLIVE (Reuters) — New famine risk haunts war-torn Sudan with El Niño-driven drought

why: Drought slowly destroys harvests, hydropower and river shipping, and drives famine and migration.
drivers: Rainfall deficits, heat, ENSO, groundwater depletion.

rubric.alert: Drought driving famine conditions, a major exporter's harvest failure, or monsoon failure across a major breadbasket.
rubric.watch: Severe drought in a major crop region, a major river at record low, or a monsoon running more than 20% below normal.
rubric.normal: No major breadbasket in severe drought.
